questions.stem: Review the client's data. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

actions.text: Stop the lisinopril and record it as an allergy
Prepare for an emergency airway at the bedside
Give IV diphenhydramine as the main treatment
Give the morning lisinopril dose with sips of water
Place the client flat in bed to rest and settle

parameters.text: Body weight measured once a day

rationale.correct: ACE inhibitor angioedema is caused by bradykinin. Stop the drug, protect the airway and watch voice, stridor and breathing.

perOption.c1: Lip and tongue swelling without hives in a client on lisinopril is bradykinin-mediated angioedema; it can occur after years of use.
perOption.c2: Anaphylaxis usually brings hives, itching and hypotension.
perOption.c3: This begins in childhood with recurrent attacks.
perOption.c4: This causes fever, sore throat and one-sided swelling.
perOption.a1: The drug must never be restarted, and ARBs are used with caution.
perOption.a2: Tongue swelling with a hoarse voice can close the airway; epinephrine and antihistamines work poorly here.
perOption.a3: Histamine is not the cause, so this does not reverse it.
perOption.a5: Lying flat can worsen airway obstruction.
perOption.p1: Show progression of upper airway swelling.
perOption.p2: Show whether the airway is compromised.

cells.text: Bases to mid-lung, then bases only

options.text: Needs follow-up before the next dose

rationale.correct: The trend shows effective diuresis; the falling potassium needs replacement before more furosemide.

perOption.b1:a: A loss of 3.4 kg is about 3.4 L of fluid removed.
perOption.b1:b: About 1 kg a day is the usual goal.
perOption.b2:a: Fewer crackles show less fluid in the lungs.
perOption.b2:b: The crackles are smaller in extent.
perOption.b3:a: Loop diuretics waste potassium; 3.2 raises dysrhythmia risk, especially with digoxin.
perOption.b3:b: It is below range and falling.
perOption.b4:a: A rise of 0.1 is within expected variation.
perOption.b4:b: AKI needs a rise of at least 0.3 mg/dL.

questions.stem: The nurse on a cardiac step-down unit receives report on four clients at 0700. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client 2 days after a stent whose heparin infusion was stopped, now with a radial site that is dry, a radial pulse 2+ and a heart rate of 92/min
A client with heart failure on a furosemide infusion who has had 1,200 mL of urine output overnight and now reports leg cramps
A client with new atrial fibrillation at 96/min on diltiazem who asks why apixaban was added this morning
A client with stable angina who rates chest discomfort 2 of 10 during a bed bath and says it went away with rest after 3 minutes

rationale.correct: Electrolyte loss after heavy diuresis threatens rhythm and life; the other clients are stable.

perOption.a: Stable access site and pulse; routine follow-up.
perOption.b: Large diuresis with new cramps suggests hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia, which can cause a fatal dysrhythmia.
perOption.c: The rate is controlled; the question is teaching that can wait.
perOption.d: Pain relieved promptly by rest is the stable pattern; it needs follow-up, not first priority.

questions.stem: The RN is working with an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) on a cardiac unit. Clients include one who had a femoral cardiac catheterization 3 hours ago, one with heart failure on daily weights and strict intake and output, and one starting a heparin infusion. Which tasks can the RN delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Weigh the client with heart failure on the same scale before breakfast
Record the intake and output for the client with heart failure
Check the femoral site and pedal pulses after catheterization
Report a blood pressure below 100 systolic to the RN at once
Adjust the heparin infusion rate after the aPTT result
Teach the client with heart failure about a low-sodium diet

rationale.correct: UAPs can measure, record and report against clear parameters; assessment, teaching and drug titration remain with the RN.

perOption.a: Standard measurement with clear direction is within the UAP's role.
perOption.b: Measuring and recording output is routine.
perOption.c: Assessment of a new post-procedure client stays with the RN.
perOption.d: Taking vital signs and reporting values the RN specifies is appropriate.
perOption.e: Medication titration is an RN responsibility.

rationale.correct: Anaphylaxis with airway threat and shock; beta blockade may make it refractory to epinephrine.

questions.stem: Select the 3 actions the nurse should anticipate first.

options.text: Stop the ceftriaxone and keep the IV line open with new tubing
Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL) into the anterolateral thigh
0.9% sodium chloride 1 to 2 L rapid IV bolus
Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV as the first drug
Epinephrine 0.5 mg of the 1 mg/mL strength by IV push
Sit the client fully upright with the legs down

rationale.correct: Stop the drug, give IM epinephrine at once and restore volume; antihistamines and steroids are add-ons.

perOption.a: Remove the trigger and keep access.
perOption.b: IM epinephrine is the first drug; the thigh gives the fastest absorption.
perOption.c: Large volumes are needed to refill the dilated vessels.
perOption.d: Antihistamines help hives but do not reverse shock or airway swelling.
perOption.e: Undiluted IV epinephrine can cause fatal dysrhythmias; IV epinephrine is given only as a dilute infusion.
perOption.f: Steroids act over hours and never replace epinephrine.
perOption.g: Upright positioning in shock can cause collapse.

exhibits.title: Rapid response team protocol for anaphylaxis
exhibits.body: Stop the suspected drug. Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM, repeat every 5 to 15 minutes. Fluid bolus. Diphenhydramine, methylprednisolone and albuterol as add-on therapy.

perOption.c: Stridor shows the airway is closing.

questions.stem: Place the nurse's steps for troubleshooting the damped arterial line in order.

items.text: Level the transducer at the phlebostatic axis and zero it
Check that the pressure bag is inflated to 300 mm Hg
Confirm the client's pressure with a manual cuff

Raise the right leg above the level of the heart
Apply a heating pad to the cold foot
Keep the leg level or slightly dependent

rationale.correct: Anticoagulate, get the surgeon and position the leg to help arterial flow; never elevate or heat an ischemic limb.

exhibits.title: Plan, 1115
exhibits.body: Heparin per protocol. Vascular surgery consult. Embolectomy planned.

questions.stem: Review the findings 6 hours after embolectomy. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the leg at heart level
Loosen the dressing around the calf
Raise the leg on two pillows to reduce the swelling
Give more morphine and reassess in 1 hour
Apply ice packs to the calf

rationale.correct: Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch with a tense calf after reperfusion is compartment syndrome.

perOption.a: These are signs of compartment syndrome, which needs urgent fasciotomy.
perOption.b: Elevation lowers arterial pressure further; dependency adds swelling.
perOption.e: Reduces flow into a compressed compartment.
perOption.f: Pain beyond expectation is the warning sign; masking it delays surgery.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

rows.text: Foot warm with a Doppler pulse

rationale.correct: Perfusion and pain have improved, but reperfusion has released myoglobin and potassium; rhabdomyolysis needs treatment.

caseStudies.title: Anaphylactic shock in a client taking a beta blocker

exhibits.title: Medical unit, 1410
exhibits.body: A 45-year-old client with cellulitis started a first dose of IV ceftriaxone at 1400. The allergy list says "penicillin: rash as a child." The client takes metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily for hypertension. At 1410 the client says, "My throat feels tight," and has hives spreading across the chest. The voice is hoarse, there is wheezing in all lung fields, and the skin is flushed and warm.

caseStudies.title: Arterial line and CVP monitoring after open AAA repair

exhibits.title: Surgical ICU, 1800
exhibits.body: A 71-year-old client returned at 1500 after open repair of an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with a cross-clamp time of 55 minutes. The client has a right radial arterial line and a central venous catheter. At 1800 the arterial line waveform is flattened with no dicrotic notch. A manual cuff pressure is 128/72 mm Hg. The client has passed a loose, bloody stool. The left foot is mottled with absent pedal pulses; the right foot is warm with Doppler pulses.

caseStudies.title: Infective endocarditis in a client who injects drugs

exhibits.title: Medical unit, admission
exhibits.body: A 32-year-old client who injects heroin has had fevers, night sweats and fatigue for 2 weeks, and now has a cough with sharp chest pain on breathing. Findings: a new holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that increases with inspiration; painless flat red spots on the soles; dark lines under several fingernails; tender nodules on two fingertips; needle tracks on both arms. A CT of the chest shows multiple small nodules in both lungs.

caseStudies.title: Acute limb ischemia and compartment syndrome

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 1100
exhibits.body: A 70-year-old client with peripheral arterial disease and atrial fibrillation stopped apixaban 2 months ago because of cost. Two hours ago the client had sudden, severe pain in the right leg at rest. The client usually gets calf cramps after walking one block. The right foot and calf are pale and cold, with numbness of the toes and weakness when moving them. No Doppler signal at the right popliteal or pedal arteries. Both lower legs are shiny and hairless with thick toenails.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
